summary: Fire lookout built inside the Civil Aeronautics Administration's beacon tower on Big Kennesaw; staffed by a state employee from 1943; the beacon tower came down in 1985.

facts.design: fire lookout built inside the airplane beacon tower on Big Kennesaw Mountain
facts.status_note: The beacon tower that held the lookout was torn down in 1985, according to the park history.

staffing.status: staffed by a state employee under a 1943 agreement; no later staffing record in the sources

access.note: Day-use national battlefield park; visitor center open 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM daily except Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day

visit.trail_note: Mountain road listed as closed to personal vehicles as of January 2026, with the park opening or closing it depending on traffic; a free shuttle runs seven days a week and parking fees still apply

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps camp established July 1 at the park; its camp foreman became park fire chief
Civil Aeronautics Administration asked to build a taller tower for its beacon; the NPS refused a new tower, allowed a stronger beacon, and the CAA agreed to put its cable underground
Construction of the fire lookout inside the CAA beacon tower began in October; the chronology gives no completion date
Cooperative agreement with the Georgia Department of Forestry; a state employee was to be stationed on the mountain as fire lookout
FAA discontinued use of the beacon tower
The beacon tower was torn down

evidence.supports: lookout built within the CAA beacon tower, camp foreman named park fire chief, telephone for reporting fires
evidence.quote: The camp foreman was designated the Park Fire Chief, all enrollees were given thorough training in suppression, and a lookout tower was established on Big Kennesaw Mountain, with a telephone for reporting fires (it was built within the tower containing the CAA beacon).

evidence.supports: CAA kept an airplane beacon on the mountain since before the park was established; it wanted a taller tower in 1939
evidence.quote: which had maintained an airplane beacon on the mountain since before the park was established, wanted to build a new, taller tower

evidence.supports: the 1939 request for a taller beacon tower
evidence.quote: The Civil Aeronautics Administration requested permission to build a new, taller tower for its airplane beacon on Big Kennesaw.

evidence.supports: NPS refused a new tower but allowed a stronger beacon
evidence.quote: Concerned about the visual effect, the NPS rejected the request for a new tower but did allow an increase in the beacon’s candlepower.

evidence.supports: CAA agreed to put its cable underground
evidence.quote: The CAA also agreed to place its cable underground.

evidence.supports: precedent set; later tower requests from AT&T, Southern Bell and the state forestry department denied
evidence.quote: With this decision, a precedent was set and subsequent requests for towers by AT&T, Southern Bell, and the Georgia State Department of Forestry were denied.

evidence.supports: Civilian Conservation Corps camp established July 1, 1938
evidence.quote: On July 1, a Civilian Conservation Corps camp was established at Kennesaw Mountain NBP.

evidence.supports: construction on the lookout inside the beacon tower began in October (1940 entries)
evidence.quote: In October, construction began on the fire lookout within the CAA beacon tower.

evidence.supports: neither the state nor the county provided fire protection before 1943
evidence.quote: because neither the state nor the county provided any kind of fire protection.

evidence.supports: in 1943 a cooperative agreement with the Georgia Department of Forestry put a state employee on the mountain
evidence.quote: This changed, however, in 1943, after the closing of the CCC camp, when the park superintendent signed a cooperative agreement with the Georgia Department of Forestry that provided for a state employee to be stationed on the mountain

evidence.supports: 1943 agreement; state employee to be stationed as fire lookout
evidence.quote: Park superintendent signed a cooperative agreement with the Georgia Department of Forestry that provided for a state employee to be stationed on Big Kennesaw as a fire lookout.

evidence.supports: the beacon was later operated by the Federal Aviation Administration
evidence.quote: The aircraft beacon was later operated by the Federal Aviation Administration.

evidence.supports: FAA beacon tower use discontinued (1984 entries)
evidence.quote: Use of the FAA beacon tower on Big Kennesaw was discontinued.

evidence.supports: FAA discontinued the tower in 1984; it was torn down in 1985
evidence.quote: In 1984, the FAA discontinued use of the tower and in 1985 it was tom down.

evidence.supports: the park is a day-use park
evidence.quote: We are a day use only park.

evidence.supports: visitor center hours, closed on three holidays
evidence.quote: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM daily *Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Years Day

evidence.supports: mountain road closed to personal vehicles as of January 2026
evidence.quote: CLOSED to personal vehicles as of January 2026.

evidence.supports: the park monitors the mountain road and may open or close it depending on traffic
evidence.quote: open or close the road depending on traffic conditions and volume

evidence.supports: free shuttle runs seven days a week; parking fees still apply
evidence.quote: A free shuttle service runs 7 days a week, parking fees still apply.

evidence.supports: Cobb County; agency National Park Service
evidence.quote: Cobb County - National Park Service

sources.title: Kennesaw Mountain NBP: An Administrative History
sources.publisher: National Park Service (copy hosted by Kennesaw Mountain Trail Club)

Operating Hours & Seasons, Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park

notes_for_editor: The October construction entry is placed in the chronology's 1940 block (no 1941 heading appears in that chronology), so the story says October 1940; a search summary had guessed 1941 and that guess was not used. The lookout's fate follows the beacon tower because the sources say the lookout was built within that tower and that the tower was torn down in 1985; the story says it 'appears' to have come down with the tower. No source read describes what remains on the summit today. The NPS admin history was read from a Kennesaw Mountain Trail Club copy; the official GovInfo copy was not read. The brief's status 'unknown' should become 'removed'. Operator before 1943 is not named in the sources; the 1943 agreement is with the Georgia Department of Forestry.
